children: Michael Dell’s family investment firm is close to acquiring The Baldwin Insurance Group
, a publicly traded insurance brokerage valued at about $4.2 billion, according to the Financial Times.

DFO Management and Baldwin could announce an agreement to take the company private as soon as next week, the report said, citing people familiar with the negotiations. The potential purchase price is expected to represent a premium to Baldwin’s current market capitalization.
If completed, the transaction would rank among the largest acquisitions undertaken by Dell’s family office.
Baldwin shares have climbed more than 23% this year, partly because of speculation that the insurance broker could attract a takeover offer.

For investors, a deal would extend the wave of private-equity and family-office investment in insurance distribution, a business prized for recurring commissions and relatively low capital requirements.

shareholders could receive a takeover premium, although the stock’s recent gains suggest investors may have already priced in part of that potential. The reported negotiations could also lift valuations across the insurance-brokerage sector by drawing attention to other possible acquisition targets.
